info.title: Basis API
info.description:
Basis cost segregation API.

**Authentication.** Every `/v1` route needs `Authorization: Bearer <Firebase ID token>`.
A user is created on first sight, in no organization: firms are invite-only.
`GET /v1/me` lists your firms and the invitations waiting for your verified email; until
you accept one, the study list and study creation answer 403 `no-firm`.

**Authorization.** Studies belong to organizations (firms). A study or firm you are not a
member of is 404, not 403; one you can see but whose action needs a higher role
(viewer < engineer < owner) is 403. Owners administer their firm under
`/v1/orgs/{org_id}`: members, roles and invitations.

**Idempotency.** `POST` and `DELETE` need an `Idempotency-Key` header (a UUID is
recommended). Retrying with the same key and body replays the stored response with
`Idempotent-Replayed: true` for 24 hours; the same key with a different body is 422; a
retry while the first request is still running is 409. Keys are scoped per user.

**Rate limits.** Per user, by default 240 reads and 60 mutations per minute; 429 with
`Retry-After`.

**Errors.** Every 4xx/5xx is `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457): `type`, `title`,
`status`, `detail`, `instance`, `request_id` (equal to the `X-Request-Id` response
header), and `errors` (one entry per field) on validation failures.

**Limits.** JSON bodies up to 1 MiB (413 beyond). Files are never sent to the API: request
a signed URL, upload to it, then confirm.

put.summary: Set or replace the study's intake (engineer)
put.description: The whole intake, validated as one document (docs/api/STUDY_RESULT.md): a non-capitalizable cost category, a land method without its input, or a use that fails the 80 % test is a 422 naming the rule. `state`/`zip` left out are filled from the appraisal's subject fields. No `Idempotency-Key` is needed. Optimistic concurrency: with `If-Match` (the `ETag` of `GET .../intake`) the write happens only while that tag is current; otherwise 412 `precondition-failed` with the current `ETag`, nothing written (re-read, reapply, retry). `If-Match: *` writes only over an existing intake. Without `If-Match` the write is accepted, unless the deployment requires it (`INTAKE_REQUIRE_IF_MATCH`: 428 `precondition-required`). Every write increments `intake_version`; the response carries the new `ETag`. The result's pricing is checked against the intake version. 409 `stale-state` on an archived study; 409 `intake-locked` once the study has started (the run, the result and the report are priced from the intake: a change is a reopen, not an edit in place).

post.summary: Approve or reject the current review stage
post.description: Records the decision and queues it for the workflow (202). A stage the study is not at, or a revision that is not its current one, is 409; so is a gate the workflow has not opened yet (`gate-not-open`: the study is at the stage but `processing` or `failed`). Each correction's `entity_type` must be one the stage accepts (appraisal_review: extraction_field, extraction_field_add; rooms_review: room, photo_room; components_review: component, component_remove, room_component, photo; assets_review: asset; a study whose `components_gate` is false has the single rooms_review: room, component, component_remove, room_component, photo) and its `entity_id` must exist in the study at the decided revision (a photo or photo_room: a photo document of the study; a room_component: the room it adds a component to); a `photo_room` `after` is exactly a `room_id` of that revision; a `component` `count` must be a whole number from 1, and a `room_component` `after` a taxonomy `label` with a `count` (optional `material`, `attachment` from their vocabularies); otherwise 422 with one `errors` entry per offending correction, located at `["body", "corrections", <index>, "entity_type" | "entity_id" | "after" | "reason"]`. A `component_remove` (an erroneous room inventory component row: `entity_id` a component of the revision, `after` exactly `{}`, `reason` required) leaves the row out of the next revision; refused: the same row removed twice or also corrected (`correction_duplicate`), a row the rejection rebuilds anyway (an inventory row of a room whose photo the same decision flags for re-analysis, or of a merged room, or a flagged photo's row: `correction_rebuilt`), a room's last inventory row (`correction_last_inventory`). It never deletes a photo's detected object (that is `DELETE .../photos/{document_id}/objects/{object_id}`). An `extraction_field_add` (an appraisal field the extraction missed: `entity_id` the extraction, `after` `{key, value_text | value_num | value_date, page, evidence}`, `reason` required) is refused for an unknown key, a value of the wrong type, a page past the PDF (`correction_value`), a key the extraction has (`correction_field_exists`: correct it with `extraction_field`) or a key added twice (`correction_duplicate`); a missing reason is `correction_reason` at `reason`.

put.description: The whole draft each time (`revision`, `comment`, `corrections`), checked exactly as `POST .../decisions` checks a decision's corrections: `entity_type` for the stage in the study's flow, `entity_id` in the named revision, values, required reasons, removals and added fields (422 with one `errors` entry per offending correction, the same `type` values). `revision` must be the study's current one and the stage undecided at it, else 409 `draft-stale`. No `Idempotency-Key` is needed. Optimistic concurrency as on the intake: with `If-Match` (the `ETag` of the `GET`; `"0"` creates only while you have none) the write happens only while that tag is current, else 412 `precondition-failed` with the current `ETag`, nothing written; without it the save is accepted. Every save increments the version; the response carries the new `ETag`. A draft is yours alone: another engineer's draft on the stage is separate. 409 `study-archived` on an archived study.

CostCategory.title: CostCategory
CostCategory.description:
A settlement-statement line. Capitalized ones add to basis (Reg. §1.263(a)-2(f),
Pub. 551 "Settlement costs"); the others are refused with the reason.

series.title: Series
series.description: `historical`: the RSMeans Historical Cost Index (Jan. 1, 1993 = 100), one national value per year; `city`: a location factor (the City Cost Index's weighted average over 100) of one city row or state.

year.title: Year
year.description: The year the value is for.

region.title: Region
region.description: `US` for a historical value; for a city row `<state>:<ZIP prefixes>` as the book prints them (`CA:900-902`), or a state code for a state value.

value.description: The index as printed, as a decimal string (`294.8`, `0.96`): up to ten digits and four decimals, above zero (the store's column scale; the pattern is the whole rule, so a client can check it).

citation.title: Citation
citation.description: Publication, table and page (or URL) as printed: what the IRS guide asks of a cost source (ATG ch. 3 C.2(2)).

derived.title: Derived
derived.description: Only for a value that is not a published RSMeans index but one you converted from another series: the conversion and its error band. Every row priced with it is flagged `cost:YEAR_INDEX_CONVERTED`; a published value for the same year outranks it.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: For a city row: `city` (required), `state`, `zip_prefixes`, `printed_page`; `estimated` for a published estimate.

CostIndexCreate.title: CostIndexCreate

obtained_by_name.description: Their name or email, or the fetcher's name.

status.description: `published`: the cost year's index is loaded (RSMeans' value, cited); `missing`: no index for the year, the latest loaded one is applied and every priced row is flagged `cost:YEAR_INDEX_MISSING`; `converted`: the year's value was converted from another series (flagged `cost:YEAR_INDEX_CONVERTED`).

factor.title: Factor
factor.description: The year factor applied (index / Jan. 1, 2020 index).

applied.title: Applied

assumption.description: The assumption written on every priced row.

engineer must enter, when the cost year has no loaded index.

unit_cost.description: Null when no cost row priced it.

Show it as recorded: never derive a base price from the rounded amounts, and never substitute today's index. Null for a row priced before the trail was recorded (`trail_recorded` false): such a row has only `source_row`.

trail_recorded.title: Trail Recorded
trail_recorded.description: Whether the row was priced with a trail (false: a legacy row, `trail` null).

unit_cost.title: Unit Cost
unit_cost.description: Per takeoff unit, at the row's base year, before the year and location factors; not rounded (it may carry more than two decimals). This, not a quotient of the rounded amounts, is the base price.

unit.title: Unit
unit.description: The takeoff unit the base is per.

table.title: Table
table.description: The configured cost table's name (`COST_TABLE_PATH`); the legacy placeholder rows were removed (EVAL_REPORT 78).

tier.title: Tier
tier.description: Always null (the legacy tiers were removed).

source.title: Source
source.description: The row's printed source (book, line, page) as the table records it; null for a legacy placeholder row, which has none.

base_year.title: Base Year
base_year.description: The year the row's costs are as of.

row_unit.title: Row Unit
row_unit.description: The unit the row is printed per.

conversion.title: Conversion
conversion.description: How the row's unit became the takeoff's (`x9 from per SF`, `x0.01 from per Sq.`); null when none was needed.

basis.title: Basis
basis.description: The cost basis (STRUCTURE_MODEL.md 9.3): `bare` (material + labor + equipment) or `installed` (with the installing contractor's overhead and profit). Rows priced before the basis was recorded read `bare`.

basis_how.title: Basis How
basis_how.description: How `unit_cost` reached the installed basis: `Total Incl O&P` (the printed column) or the square-foot section's markups; null on the bare basis.

markup.description: The square-foot model's general contractor's overhead and profit spread on the row: `unit_cost x (1 + rate)` is what the year and location factors multiply. Null when none.

CostTrailBaseOut.title: CostTrailBaseOut
CostTrailBaseOut.description: The base unit cost exactly as multiplied, and the cost row it came from.

amount.title: Amount

inputs.title: Inputs

CostTrailBuildingOut.title: CostTrailBuildingOut

city.title: City

zip_prefixes.title: Zip Prefixes

store.description: The city row's store row; null for a state mean or the book file's row.

CostTrailLocationOut.title: CostTrailLocationOut
CostTrailLocationOut.description: The location factor exactly as used, with the row(s) it came from.

CostTrailMarkupOut.description: A pro-rata indirect cost on the row (ATG ch. 4 C.11(2)).

priced_per.title: Priced Per

missing.title: Missing
missing.description: What the result lacks: `intake` (no basis without it), `building_rcn` (no appraisal cost approach and no living area), `depreciation` (no rate), `allocation` (nothing priced, or the reconciliation is not within tolerance), `cost_index` (no loaded index for the cost year: `cost_index` says which value to enter), `repricing` (the recorded pricing is stale: `pricing` says why), `blockers` (an input the dollars need is missing: `blockers` lists each), or nothing.

blockers.title: Blockers
blockers.description: Every reason the allocation is withheld because an input is missing, an asset is unpriced or unclassified, or the building model stands on an assumed input (EVAL_REPORT 78): no report is rendered or signed while one remains.

cost_index.description: The time index the dollars rest on; null without structure inputs.

not_produced.title: Not Produced
not_produced.description: Concealed systems with no priced row in this schedule, so the gap to the basis is explicit.

pricing.description: What the revision's dollars were priced with (recorded on its cost rows) against what the study's current intake and index store give. The structure, the reconciliation and the allocation use the recorded pricing, never a newer index. When `stale`, the allocation is withheld (`missing` lists `repricing`) until a reprice builds a revision priced with the current inputs. Null without structure inputs.

photo_count.title: Photo Count
photo_count.description: The most counted instances of the label in one photo of the room: SAM 3's counted instances plus the engineers' manual ones.

suggested.title: Suggested
suggested.description: max(`inventory_count`, `photo_count`): a room has at least as many as one photo shows. A suggestion for the engineer to confirm with a `component` (`count`) or `room_component` correction; nothing changes by itself.

method.title: Method
method.description: How the quantity was measured: `count`, `area` or `perimeter` (the takeoff inputs' `method`); null for a takeoff stored without it.

inputs.title: Inputs
inputs.description: The takeoff inputs exactly as stored when the asset was measured: the room area and its source, the appraisal fields, the cost index sources, an engineer's `asset_correction`, a concealed row's `label` and `system`. Keys vary by takeoff; show them, do not compute from them.

assumptions.title: Assumptions

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to get the next page; null on the last page.

analyzed.title: Analyzed
analyzed.description: True: the analysis ran and the model put the photo in no room. False: the analysis never produced a result for this photo (it failed for good, the budget could not cover it, or it has not run yet), so none of its components are counted. Either way the photo is in no room of this revision; flag it for re-analysis with a `photo` correction at the rooms gate.
